title: feat(dsc): add ZoomIt settings function data

status.label: Review draft ready
status.detail: Three grounded inline prose comments identify unsupported ZoomIt setting values, a lost combined recording-scale update, and missing release-mode bounds validation for fixed-size native settings.

next_action: Review and approve the proposed inline comments. Nothing has been posted upstream.

proposed_comments.body:
### Reject out-of-range ZoomIt values

**Severity:** `high`

`ZoominSliderLevel` is exposed as an unconstrained `IntProperty` and this new `SetState` path forwards it to the native settings writer; ZoomIt later indexes the six-entry `g_ZoomLevels` array directly with that value, so a value of 6 or greater can read past the array. `RecordFormat` is likewise an unconstrained string, while the interop maps every value other than `GIF` to MP4, silently treating unsupported input as a valid format. Validate numeric bounds and allowed format values before persisting, and return a validation error instead of accepting unsupported DSC input.

confidence.rationale: The added save path forwards the declared setting directly; the pinned native implementation maps it to a six-entry index and accepts every non-GIF format as MP4.

proposed_comments.body:
### Preserve requested scaling during a format change

**Severity:** `medium`

When DSC sets `RecordFormat` and `RecordScaling` together, `SetState` sends the complete settings object in one native call. The native writer switches `g_RecordScaling` to the target format's cached value and sets `formatChanged`, then skips the supplied `RecordScaling` value whenever that flag is true, so the explicit scale is not applied. Preserve the requested scale across the format transition and cover the combined update with a regression test.

confidence.rationale: The pinned writer explicitly suppresses the supplied scaling value whenever the same save changes format; the regression scenario is covered by the converged candidate tests.

proposed_comments.body:
### Validate fixed-size settings before copying

**Severity:** `high`

The new DSC path forwards caller-supplied settings to `SaveSettingsJson`; the interop copies string values into fixed-size buffers with `_tcscpy_s` and decodes `Font` before `memcpy`, but its size check is only an `assert`. In release builds an oversized string can invoke the secure-CRT invalid-parameter path, and oversized decoded font data can write beyond `g_LogFont`. Validate string capacity and require the decoded binary size to match the destination before the native save proceeds, returning an explicit input error for invalid values.

confidence.rationale: The new call path accepts string-backed Font data and reaches native fixed-size copies; the binary-size condition is debug-only while memcpy uses the supplied length.
